title: Prompt telemetry and response lineage specification
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This specification defines a minimal, extendable telemetry contract that links incoming prompts and correlated context to generated responses across Redwood's serving surfaces. The goal is to enable reliable debugging, quality-tracking, and cost attribution while preserving user privacy and minimizing ingestion costs.

Purpose:
- Make it possible to reconstruct the exact prompt->response path for post-hoc debugging and evals.
- Provide a stable, low-cardinality set of keys for aggregation and dashboarding.
- Define sampling tiers and PII-mitigation that satisfy compliance and cost constraints.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated, private runtime sidecars).
- Covers producer-side instrumentation, ingestion pipeline expectations, storage/retention, and query patterns.
- Does NOT mandate model output schemas; it only requires lineage metadata alongside outputs.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for full request/trace logs. High-volume raw traces are out-of-scope and remain handled by trace infrastructure.
- We do not require storing unredacted customer prompt payloads in long-term indexes.

Key concepts and identifiers:
- interaction_id: stable UUID for a single user request from ingress to final stored response. Every telemetry event for the same request MUST carry the same interaction_id.
- prompt_id: per-prompt stable id derived from the prompt (see prompt hashing). Not guaranteed to be unique across users; used for cache/prefix analytics.
- response_id: unique UUID for the generated response variant. Multiple response events (candidates, reranks) may exist per interaction_id.
- lineage_key: short composite key for fast joins: {service}:{model}:{response_id} (example: "ingress:rdw-ggml-13b:resp-1a2b").
- prompt_hash: SHA256 truncated to 16 hex chars. Used for dedup and similarity telemetry without exposing full prompt text.

Event schema (core fields):
| field | type | required | description |
|---|---:|:---:|---|
| event_type | string | required | one of: "prompt.received", "prompt.forwarded", "model.generated", "response.emitted", "response.candidate", "rerank.scored" |
| timestamp_utc | string (RFC3339) | required | event wall-clock time in UTC |
| interaction_id | string | required | GUID that ties the request end-to-end |
| response_id | string | conditional | present for any model/response event |
| prompt_id | string | recommended | stable id for prompt content groupings |
| prompt_hash | string | recommended | truncated SHA256 of prompt (PII-free) |
| model | string | required | canonical model name and variant (e.g., "rw-instruct-13b-v2-8q") |
| stage | string | required | producer stage (ingress, router, runtime, postproc) |
| status | string | required | "ok", "partial", "error" |
| cost_tokens | integer | optional | token accounting for this event (model-specific) |
| trace_id | string | optional | internal trace id (for tracing systems) |
| sample_rate | number | optional | fraction [0.0-1.0] used by producer for sampling this event |

Storage and retention:
- Ingest pipeline: all core events are written to the ingestion topic "telemetry.events" with schema version header "t-v:1". Processors downstream are expected to honor schema versioning.
- Short-term index: partitioned by day into the fast search cluster (index prefix: telemetry_live-YYYYMMDD). Retention: 30 days.
- Long-term store: sampled and PII-processed snapshots are exported to telemetry-archive S3 (prefix: s3://telemetry-archive/lineage/). Retention: 365 days for sampled artifacts; 7 years for security/audit artifacts when explicitly flagged.
- Freshness SLO: 99% of prompt.received events available in telemetry_live within 90s of ingestion. Ownership: observability-team / telemetry-platform.

Privacy and PII handling:
1) Default collection: producers SHOULD NOT include full prompt text in telemetry_live. Prompt text MAY be included for response.emitted events only if the request is marked "consent=true".
2) Prompt hashing: compute prompt_hash = hex(truncate(SHA256(normalize(prompt)), 16)). Normalization: strip whitespace, remove direct user identifiers (email-looking tokens), lowercase.
3) Redaction policy: any detected credit-card numbers, SSNs, or other sensitive patterns must be redacted before emitting any telemetry event. Use the redact-service API or client SDK helpers.
4) Opt-out: customers can set telemetry.write=false at the tenant level; producers must adhere within 30s of flag change. Private deployments may override per-customer retention.

Sampling and tiering:
- Tier definitions:
  - Debug-level (sample_rate=1.0): capture full prompt text and all events, only for canaries, customer repros, and explicit support captures.
  - Diagnostic-level (sample_rate=0.1): capture prompt_hash + truncated prompt preview (first 128 chars) and model outputs. Used for progressive QA.
  - Metrics-level (sample_rate=0.01): capture metadata only (ids, model, tokens, status) for aggregate dashboards and cost attribution.
- Sampling rules:
  1) Errors (status != "ok") must be upsampled: ensure effective rate >= 50 events/day per distinct error type for the service.
  2) Cold-start, prewarming, and performance degradation events must use sample_rate=1.0 for the first 5m after any scaling event.
  3) Recording full prompt text is allowed only under Debug-level sampling or explicit consent.

Event versioning and backward compatibility:
- Schema versions are carried in the record header "t-schema". Producers MUST include this header. Consumers should ignore unknown fields.
- Backwards-compatible changes: adding optional fields, adding new enum values.
- Breaking changes: removing required fields or renaming core ids. These require an ADR and a 6-week rollout plan.

Producer implementation checklist:
1) Add interaction_id generation at ingress: use UUIDv4, attached to request context.
2) Compute prompt_id and prompt_hash at the earliest safe point (ingress or edge).
3) Emit prompt.received with sample_rate and stage=ingress.
4) Emit model.generated events for each candidate with response_id and model metadata.
5) Emit response.emitted with final response_id and cost_tokens.
6) Ensure any included prompt text is redacted and consent-checked.
7) Attach trace_id and span context when available.
8) Increment local counters for retry and fallback reasons for later aggregation.

Consumer and tooling guidance:
- Dashboards to build:
  - Lineage table: latest 1000 interactions with interaction_id, prompt_id, model, status, latency, response_id.
  - Response quality heatmap: prompt_hash frequency vs. rerank rate.
  - Cost funnel: tokens charged per stage aggregated by model and customer tier.
- Debug workflow (ordered steps):
  1) Query telemetry_live for interaction_id (fast index).
  2) If missing, search telemetry-archive for prompt_hash or time window.
  3) Reconstruct timeline by ordering events by timestamp_utc.
  4) If prompt text absent, request a debug capture from customer or enable Debug-level sampling temporarily.

Query examples (Elasticsearch / KQL fragments):
- Find errors for model X in last hour:
  event_type: "response.emitted" AND model: "rw-instruct-13b-v2-8q" AND status: "error" | sort timestamp_utc desc
- Correlate prompt_hash to responses in last 7 days:
  prompt_hash: "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8" | terms response_id | top 50

Rollout and migration plan:
- Phase 0 (1 week): SDK and runtime-sidecar instrumented to emit schema v1 events to a shadow topic. No downstream consumers read this.
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Enable consumers to read v1 (feature-flagged) and validate field coverage using the schema-checker job.
- Phase 2 (1 week): Start producing live v1 for 5% of traffic with upsampling of errors.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): Ramp to 25%, then to 100% once dashboards and alerts validate correctness.
- Coordinators: telemetry-platform, runtime-team, and customer-success for any tenant impacts.

SLOs and alerts:
- Telemetry ingestion latency: 99th percentile < 90s (alert if > 120s for 5m).
- Schema validity: >=99.9% of events must pass schema checker for a given day.
- Missing lineage alert: if >0.1% of response.emitted events lack interaction_id for 1h, pager oncall.

Costs and expected volumes (approx):
- Global baseline: 50M prompt.received events/day across all deployment modes (estimate). With Metrics-level sampling at 1%, we expect ~0.5M records/day into telemetry_live.
- Storage estimate (fast index): ~2.5 TB/month at 1% sampling. Long-term snapshots depend on sampling tier.

Appendix: example telemetry payloads
- model.generated (sample):
{
  "t-schema": "1",
  "event_type": "model.generated",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-02-28T18:12:34.123Z",
  "interaction_id": "0f7b9a2c-3d4e-4a6a-9dcb-1a2b3c4d5e6f",
  "response_id": "resp-1a2b3c",
  "prompt_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8",
  "model": "rw-instruct-13b-v2-8q",
  "stage": "runtime",
  "status": "ok",
  "cost_tokens": 42,
  "sample_rate": 0.01
}

- response.emitted (debug-level with prompt preview):
{
  "t-schema": "1",
  "event_type": "response.emitted",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-02-28T18:12:34.456Z",
  "interaction_id": "0f7b9a2c-3d4e-4a6a-9dcb-1a2b3c4d5e6f",
  "response_id": "resp-1a2b3c",
  "prompt_preview": "when will the next earnings call be for ACME corp...",
  "model": "rw-instruct-13b-v2-8q",
  "stage": "postproc",
  "status": "ok",
  "cost_tokens": 42,
  "sample_rate": 1.0
}

Ownership and contacts:
- Spec steward: Aisha Patel (eng) — primary contact for clarifications and ADR submissions.
- Implementation owners: runtime-team (producer wiring), telemetry-platform (ingestion + schema-checker), observability-team (dashboards + alerts).

FAQ:
Q: Why not store full prompt text by default?
A: Full prompt retention increases privacy risk and ingestion cost. We use prompt_hash + tiered sampling to balance visibility with safety.

Q: How do I debug a customer issue if the prompt text is not available?
A: Use the debug capture workflow: enable Debug-level sampling for the specific tenant and time window, or request a customer-provided reproducible prompt.
